It uses only Node.js 26 built-ins (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`) and plain JavaScript ES modules.\n\n## Starting and verifying the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` runs `node server.js` in the foreground. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` and reads the port from the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `3000`.\n\nVerify it is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# {\"ok\":true}\n```\n\n## Entry point and major files\n\n- **`server.js`** — Entry point. Creates the HTTP server, wires the route table via `lib/router.js`, resets the SQLite database with `db.resetDb()`, and starts listening.\n- **`lib/router.js`** — Minimal HTTP router. Routes are registered with `.get()`, `.post()`, and `.put()` and matched by HTTP method and regex. Captured path segments are spread as positional arguments to the handler.\n- **`lib/db.js`** — Persistence layer. Owns the SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection, the schema, and all CRUD operations. Schema creation is centralized in `ensureSchema()` and used by both initialization and reset. The `TABLE_NAMES` array is kept in dependency order so the reset path can drop child tables before parents. JSON columns are deserialized with the shared `parseJson()` helper.\n- **`lib/handlers.js`** — HTTP request handlers, organized by domain (health, storage, auth, dice, checks, characters, PHB rules, combat, compendium, campaigns, DM helpers, and play campaigns). Handlers are kept thin: they validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Private helpers inside the module reduce duplication in the play-campaign surface: `loadPlayCampaign`, `publicNarration`, and `resolveNextTurn`.\n- **`lib/domain.js`** — Pure business logic and validation: dice parsing, encounter XP, initiative ordering, ability modifiers, proficiency bonus, auth hashing, and shared validation helpers (`isNonEmptyString`, `isPositiveInteger`, `isValidSlug`, etc.). Shared constants such as `ABILITY_NAMES` live here.\n- **`lib/http.js`** — Shared HTTP utilities: body reading, JSON responses, and common error helpers (`badRequest`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `notFound`, `methodNotAllowed`, `conflict`).\n- **`run.sh`** — Foreground startup script.\n\n## State, persistence, and request routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- SQLite database file: `game.db` in the project root.\n- Schema version is fixed at `1` and exposed via `/v1/storage/status`.\n- Tables: `users`, `combat_sessions`, `monsters`, `items`, `campaigns`, `characters`, `events`, `factions`, `npcs`, `quests`, `campaign_inventory`, `character_equipment`, `crafting_projects`, `campaign_sessions`, `session_attendance`, `play_campaigns`, `play_members`, `play_narrations`.\n- JSON arrays/objects (initiative order, combat conditions, monster tags, quest milestones, session agendas, play-campaign queues) are serialized to `TEXT` columns with `JSON.stringify` and deserialized with `JSON.parse` via the shared `parseJson()` helper in `lib/db.js`.\n- `/v1/storage/reset` drops all tables and recreates them. This is the only destructive endpoint and is intended for tests. The drop order follows the dependency order in `lib/db.js` so foreign-key constraints are satisfied.\n\n### Request routing\n\n`server.js` builds a `Router` from `lib/router.js`. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. The route table is grouped by domain in `server.js`, but the order within each domain is preserved from previous stages so that parameterized routes (e.g., `/v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`) are still registered before their more general parents (`/v1/combat/sessions`).\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET`, `DELETE`, or any method other than `POST`/`PUT` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` or `PUT` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- `POST` or `PUT` with a matching route reads the body and runs the handler.\n\n`POST`/`PUT` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson` via `lib/handlers.js::requireBody`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n### Module and data-flow boundaries\n\n```\n server.js   ──▶  lib/router.js  ──▶  lib/handlers.js\n                                     │\n                                     ▼\n              ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────┐\n              ▼                                   ▼\n       lib/db.js                            lib/domain.js\n    (SQLite + schema)                      (pure logic)\n              │\n              ▼\n       lib/http.js\n  (responses + body reading)\n```\n\n- `server.js` only routes and starts the server.\n- `lib/router.js` only matches methods/patterns and reads bodies for POST/PUT.\n- `lib/handlers.js` only validates HTTP input, calls the DB/domain layer, and serializes responses.\n- `lib/db.js` only talks to SQLite and maps rows to/from JS objects.\n- `lib/domain.js` has no side effects and no knowledge of HTTP or SQLite.\n- `lib/http.js` only provides HTTP utilities and does not depend on the The only source of randomness is `crypto.randomBytes` for password salts.\n\nInternal structure may change as long as every observable behavior remains identical.\n\n## Conventions for safely extending and testing the codebase\n\n- **Keep handlers thin**: handlers validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Place parameterized routes before general ones that could shadow them. Any changes must keep status codes and JSON keys identical.\n- **Centralize schema changes**: when adding or changing tables, update `lib/db.js` only. Use the `parseJson()` helper when deserializing JSON columns.\n- **JSON bodies**: all handlers use `requireBody` from `lib/handlers.js`, which wraps `lib/http.js::parseJson`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n- **Errors**: `badRequest` → `400 { error }`, `unauthorized` → `401 { error }`, `forbidden` → `403 { error }`, `notFound` → `404 { error: 'not found' }`, `methodNotAllowed` → `405 { error: 'method not allowed' }`, `conflict` → `409 { error }`. Uncaught errors log to stderr and return `500 { error: 'internal server error' }`.\n- **No external dependencies**: do not add npm packages or TypeScript.
